title: Retryer.call's int attempt counter wraps after 2^31-1 attempts: non-positive attempt numbers, RetryException count truncated to int, attempt-based waits jump
cause: Retryer.call counts attempts in an int (for (int attemptNumber = 1; ; attemptNumber++), Retryer.java:157) that silently overflows. The wrapped value is widened into the long Attempt.getAttemptNumber() (documented 'starting from 1') of every ResultAttempt/ExceptionAttempt and stored in RetryException's int numberOfFailedAttempts (Retryer.java:174, :181; RetryException.java:34, 44-46).
trigger: One call() makes more than 2^31-1 rejected attempts: a stop strategy that does not stop by attempt count (neverStop, the builder default; stopAfterDelay; a custom one) and a rejection predicate that keeps rejecting (e.g. polling a condition). With the builder defaults (noWait, Thread.sleep(0)) this host reached the wrap after about 59 minutes; with a BlockStrategy that skips the Thread.sleep(0) yield, after about 78 s.
consequence: Attempt 2,147,483,648 is passed to listeners, stop and wait strategies with getAttemptNumber() = -2,147,483,648; numbers then run through 0 and restart at 1 after 2^32 attempts, so no observer ever sees a number above 2,147,483,647. RetryException.getNumberOfFailedAttempts() and its message report (int) of the real count (144,727,207 for 4,439,694,503 failed attempts; -916,908,789 for 3,378,058,507 when stopAfterDelay ends the call). With incrementingWait(50 ms, -10 ms) the built-in strategy asks for a 21,474,836,540 ms (248.6-day) sleep right at the wrap. exponentialWait collapses to 0 at the wrap but needs at least 2^31 x 2 ms (49.7 days) of sleeping to get there; the Fibonacci collapse is not reachable in practice.
premises: A single call() can make more than 2^31-1 attempts: the configured stop strategy does not stop by attempt count (neverStop, the builder default; stopAfterDelay; or a custom strategy) and the rejection predicate keeps rejecting.
stopAfterAttempt(int) cannot reach the wrap because its limit is an int <= Integer.MAX_VALUE.
Nothing downstream re-derives or corrects the count: RetryException.numberOfFailedAttempts is a final int and Attempt numbers are passed through unchanged.

With fibonacciWait (O(n) fib per attempt, ~20 years of CPU to reach the wrap) or incrementingWait with a positive increment (quadratic total sleep) the wrap is not reachable in practice; exponentialWait needs at least 2^31 x 2 ms of real sleeping.
Reproduced on JDK 21 with --release 8 against Guava 22.0; the counter arithmetic is Java int overflow and does not depend on the JDK or Guava version.
